title: Beyond-Birthday-Bound Security for Linear Tweakable Even-Mansour
summary: A known 4-round linear TEM construction reaches 2n/3-bit security, while whether linear tweakable Even-Mansour can achieve beyond-birthday-bound security remains open.

formal_statement.body: A tweakable Even--Mansour (TEM) construction using linear key-tweak mixing, an $n$-bit key, and an $n$-bit tweak is known to achieve $2n/3$-bit security in a 4-round instance. The unresolved question is whether a TEM construction with linear mixing, an $n$-bit key, and an $n$-bit tweak can achieve security beyond the birthday bound.

scope.domain: Design of symmetric-cryptographic tweakable block-cipher constructions based on Even-Mansour.
parameters: Linear key-tweak mixing: mixing-function design constraint
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether a tweakable Even-Mansour construction with linear mixing, an n-bit key, and an n-bit tweak can achieve security beyond the birthday bound.

citations.label: Minimizing the Two-Round Tweakable Even-Mansour Cipher

progress.summary: The source presents this explicitly as an open problem after noting that a 4-round TEM with linear key-tweak mixing achieves 2n/3-bit security. It states that realizing beyond-birthday-bound security for a TEM with an n-bit key and n-bit tweak remains open.
citation_labels: Avijit Dutta et al., Minimizing the Two-Round Tweakable Even-Mansour Cipher
